sources.title: Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000
sources.summary: For a visa refusal that caused a qualifying student default, s 47E uses the default day. For failure to start, that day is the agreed starting day, subject to s 47A conditions. Other agreement claims have a different trigger under s 47D(4).

sources.title: Calculation of Refund Instrument 2024
sources.summary: For visa refusal causing failure to start, course fees include tuition and non-tuition fees received by the provider. The deduction is the lesser of 5% of course fees received before default and AUD 500. Schedule 1 repeals the 2014 specification.

sources.title: Department of Education · International students / TPS
sources.summary: TPS may assist when a provider fails to meet its obligations after a default. Statutory conditions must be checked for the individual case.

sources.title: Department of Education · International providers / TPS
sources.summary: Provider guidance describes default obligations. Its written-agreement paragraph still refers to the repealed 2014 specification; RefundPath instead uses the 2024 instrument.

sources.title: Commonwealth Ombudsman · International student complaints
sources.section: What we can do / other complaint services
sources.summary: Higher education complaints may go to the National Student Ombudsman; private VET to the Commonwealth Ombudsman’s Overseas Student team; public VET to a state or territory ombudsman. The student must confirm jurisdiction.

rules.section: ESOS Act s 47E(3), s 5 and s 47A(1)(a)
